title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy MCG11-002
caption: Galaxy MCG+08-11-002, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: MCG+08-11-002 · constellation Auriga · about 250 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A dark band of dust lies across the center of MCG+08-11-002, giving this odd-looking galaxy the appearance of a black eye. Around it, the frame is crowded with foreground stars, because the galaxy lies near the Milky Way's plane on the sky, so we look at it through our own galaxy's crowded disc.

Scientists believe the galaxy is what remains of an earlier collision between two separate galaxies. The dust band sits in front of the galaxy's center and absorbs its light, which is what gives the galaxy its black-eye look.

MCG+08-11-002 lies about 250 million light-years away in Auriga, the Charioteer. The image is part of a set of 59 colliding and merging galaxies that NASA released in April 2008 for the telescope's 18th anniversary, a collection meant to show mergers at many stages.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colors were assigned.
understand.eye: The 36-minute exposure gathers far more light than the eye can.

explore: According to NASA, galaxy collisions unfold over several hundred million years, far too slowly to see change in a human lifetime. Most of the 2008 anniversary images came from GOALS, the Great Observatories All-sky LIRG Survey, which studies luminous and ultra-luminous infrared galaxies.
alt: A galaxy with a dark band of dust across its center, surrounded by many foreground stars.
